title: Convertible mittens in DK wool
subtitle: Full mitten with a flip-top flap that folds back to expose the fingers.
excerpt: Mittens with a hinged flap that folds back over the fingers to convert to a fingerless mitt. DK weight, worked in the round, gusseted thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 12th series (1880s), §Fold-back mittens. Convertible or flip-top mittens with a hinged flap appear in several late-Victorian knitting publications. The basic construction is out of UK and EU copyright.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rounds = 10 × 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb construction where a wedge of extra stitches is increased over several rounds at the thumb position. The gusset stitches are placed on waste yarn while the hand continues, then worked as the thumb. This gives a more comfortable fit at the base of the thumb than an afterthought construction.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

Working new live stitches along an existing knitted edge by inserting the needle through the fabric and pulling a loop of yarn through. Used here to attach the flip-top flap to the finger-opening edge.

content.text: Mittens with a hinged flap that folds back to expose the fingers, sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
These are worked in the round using
magic loop
on a long circular. The hand is worked as a standard stocking stitch mitten with a
gusseted thumb

. At the finger-opening row the work splits: the palm stitches bind off and the back-of-hand stitches continue upward as the flap. The flap is worked flat, decreasing at each side to form a rounded top. It folds over the fingers and is held in place with a press stud or button. Budget about 120 g (260 m / 285 yards) of DK wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 120 g (about 260 m / 285 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 4 — 1 for beginning of round, 2 for gusset, 1 to mark the palm/back-of-hand split

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 40 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the gusset

items.name: Press studs or buttons
items.qty: 2 — to fasten the flap when folded back

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 30 rounds to 10 cm over stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked. The flap works at the same gauge because it is knitted in the same stitch.
Stitches used
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count and measurement reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 36 (40, 44) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 2×2 rib (k2, p2) for 24 (26, 28) rounds.
Thumb gusset

Switch to stocking stitch. Place gusset markers flanking the first 2 stitches of the round. Increase round: SM, M1R, k2, M1L, SM, knit to end. Work 2 plain rounds. Repeat 3 times more. Gusset holds 10 (10, 12) stitches.
Place the 10 (10, 12) gusset stitches on waste yarn and cast on 2 bridging stitches over the gap. Total hand stitches: 38 (42, 46).
Hand body
Work in stocking stitch for 18 (20, 22) rounds. The hand measures about 14 (16, 18) cm from the top of the cuff.
Finger-opening split
The round now divides into palm and flap. The palm stitches are the first 18 (20, 22) stitches (half the total). The back-of-hand stitches become the flap.
Bind off the 18 (20, 22) palm stitches. The remaining 20 (22, 24) back-of-hand stitches continue as the flap, worked flat from this point.
Flap
Working flat: Row 1 (RS) knit. Row 2 (WS) purl. Work 8 (10, 10) plain rows.
Top shaping: Decrease row (RS): k1, ssk, knit to last 3 stitches, k2tog, k1. Work 1 WS row. Repeat until 8 (8, 10) stitches remain. Bind off.
Pick up and knit a facing for the finger edge:
pick up and knit
1 stitch per bound-off stitch along the palm bind-off edge. Work 4 rows of 1×1 rib, then bind off in rib. Fold to the wrong side and slip-stitch down to neaten the opening.
Thumb

Return the 10 (10, 12) gusset stitches to the needles and pick up 2 stitches from the bridging cast-on. Work 10 (12, 12) rounds of stocking stitch. Work a decrease round: (k1, k2tog) across. Draw yarn through remaining stitches to close.
Common faults
Flap too short to cover the fingers: the finger-opening split was made too early. The hand body should measure at least 14 (16, 18) cm from the cuff top before splitting.
Flap puckers at the sides: the decreases were not matched left and right. The ssk (left-leaning) sits at the start and the k2tog (right-leaning) sits at the end of each decrease row.
Finishing
Weave in all tails. Sew a press stud or button at the base of the flap to hold it when folded back.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with a wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
Adding a cable or Fair Isle band to the flap gives the mitten more visual weight and justifies the extra fabric. The construction stays the same.
